We've seen multiple reports about the use of Apple Vision Pro in medical settings. This week, Stryker announced the completion of the world's first surgery performed using an innovative application on Vision Pro.

The procedure was a hip arthroscopy, using an application called SportSuite Vision, which brings 'critical digital content into the surgeon's virtual space,' including arthroscopic imaging, HipCheck, HipMap, and CT imaging.

Here's Stryker's description of the application:

SportSuite Vision brings critical digital content into the surgeon's visual space, allowing them to see both physical objects and digital tools such as arthroscopic imaging, HipCheck, HipMap, and CT imaging simultaneously in the operating room. When performing arthroscopic surgery, surgeons often rely on multiple monitors positioned at different locations in the OR to access imaging and surgical data. By consolidating multiple data sources into the surgeon's field of view, this technology can reduce reliance on traditional monitors and support a more streamlined, ergonomic surgical workflow.

SportSuite Vision received FDA De Novo authorization on July 17. Stryker says this is the first application approved by the FDA for use during surgery on Vision Pro.
